itemB: EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer rubber single-ply membrane)

verdict.winner: TPO wins on a cooling-load Newark flat roof; EPDM wins on ponding, chemical, or budget roofs.
verdict.reasoning: TPO beats EPDM when the building runs a summer cooling load, because TPO's white reflective surface stays over 50 degrees F cooler than a conventional roof per the DOE and cuts peak cooling demand 11-27% per the EPA; TPO seams are heat-welded per the NRCA.
verdict.alternate: EPDM beats TPO when the roof faces standing water, rooftop chemical exposure, or a tighter budget, because EPDM is an inert flexible rubber that installs at $7.00-$10.00 per square foot in NJ per Josten Roofing, below TPO's $8.00-$12.00.

keyFacts: TPO installs at $8.00-$12.00 per square foot in NJ; EPDM installs cheaper at $7.00-$10.00 per square foot, per Josten Roofing.
TPO lasts 7-20 years on the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, commonly cited at 15-25 years in practice.
EPDM lasts 15-25 years per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, with a service-life study citing 25-30 years.
White TPO carries a CRRC-listed solar reflectance near 0.70-0.85 measured by ASTM C1549.
A reflective roof surface stays over 50 degrees F cooler than a conventional roof, per the DOE.
A reflective TPO surface cuts peak cooling demand by 11-27% in air-conditioned buildings per the EPA, which is a peak-demand reduction, not a guaranteed annual bill cut.
Newark sits in IRC Climate Zone 4A-5, a heating-dominated mixed climate, so a reflective TPO roof carries a winter heating penalty that offsets part of the summer gain, per the DOE.
EPDM's black carbon-filled surface absorbs heat and resists UV; black EPDM outlasts white EPDM because the carbon black acts as a UV stabilizer, per industry guidance.
TPO seams are heat-welded into a fused thermoplastic bond; EPDM seams are taped or adhered, per the NRCA.
TPO's dominant failure mode is welded-seam failure (a defective weld opens the leak path); EPDM's dominant failure mode is seam separation driven by adhesive aging and membrane shrinkage.
EPDM repairs faster in the field by clean-prime-patch (cleaned, primed, and patched with adhesive), while a permanent TPO repair requires heat-welding equipment.
A small membrane patch runs $300-$500, per Modernize.
A failing section of either TPO or EPDM membrane replaces for $500-$1,000, per Modernize.
Both membranes require NRCA positive drainage of at least 1/4 inch per foot (about 2%) because ponding water stresses every seam and accelerates membrane deterioration on either sheet.
EPDM, as an inert flexible rubber, resists rooftop chemical exposure and flexes around heavy rooftop equipment better than TPO, which needs walk pads and equipment supports to protect the membrane.
sources: NRCA (National Roofing Contractors Association) - single-ply membrane definitions, heat-welded vs taped seams, minimum 1/4-inch-per-foot design slope
InterNACHI life-expectancy chart - TPO 7-20 years, EPDM 15-25 years
Josten Roofing - NJ installed cost ranges (TPO $8-$12/sq ft, EPDM $7-$10/sq ft)
EPA - reflective roof cuts peak cooling demand 11-27% in air-conditioned buildings
DOE (U.S. Department of Energy) - reflective roof stays 50+ degrees F cooler, IRC Climate Zone 4A-5 heating-dominated, winter heating penalty
CRRC (Cool Roof Rating Council) - listed solar reflectance for white TPO
ASTM C1549 - solar reflectance test method
Industry guidance - carbon black as UV stabilizer in black EPDM
njContext: TPO installs at $8.00-$12.00 per square foot in NJ; EPDM at $7.00-$10.00 per square foot, per Josten Roofing.
Both TPO and EPDM install to the same NJ low-slope drainage rule: NRCA minimum design slope of 1/4 inch per foot (about 2%) so water drains rather than ponds.

Newark and the surrounding Essex County (East Orange, Bloomfield) sit in IRC Climate Zone 4A-5, a heating-dominated mixed climate per the DOE; a reflective TPO roof cuts peak summer cooling demand but carries a winter heating penalty, so net annual benefit depends on insulation and exposure.

On Newark/Essex County homes, EPDM fits most residential flat sections (rear additions, sun porches, attached garages) because it installs fast by clean-prime-patch and costs less; black EPDM blends with traditional Essex County rooflines.

TPO suits an Essex County commercial roof carrying air-conditioning load (peak cooling demand down 11-27% per EPA); EPDM suits a warehouse, storage, or low-HVAC building where reflectance adds no measurable benefit and chemical/equipment resistance matters.
Newark Quality Roofing installs tapered insulation to move water off either membrane and details both membranes for foot traffic at every commercial penetration.
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (NJ HIC, N.J.S.A. 56:8-136), insured, offering a free written estimate, that installs both TPO and EPDM single-ply membranes on low-slope Essex County roofs. NQR's role is matching the membrane to the building: TPO on cooling-load roofs for its CRRC-listed reflectance and heat-welded seams, EPDM on ponding/chemical/budget roofs for its inert-rubber durability and lower NJ cost, plus tapered insulation for NRCA positive drainage. Warranty framing is honest and two-part: a manufacturer material warranty on the membrane plus NQR's own written workmanship warranty on the installation; never imply manufacturer certification tiers or a roofing license NJ does not issue. This is not a solar page, so no solar/ITC framing applies.
defabToKill: BUYER'S GUIDE - 'reducing cooling costs by 15-30% during NJ summers': invented figure and wrong metric. Gold says 11-27% peak cooling DEMAND per EPA (not cost, not 15-30%). Replace with gold's 11-27% peak-demand-per-EPA figure.
BUYER'S GUIDE - 'EPDM costs $4.50-$7.50 per sq ft installed... TPO runs $5.50-$9.00': invented cost ranges contradicting gold. Gold/Josten: EPDM $7-$10, TPO $8-$12 per sq ft.
BUYER'S GUIDE - 'On a 10,000 sq ft commercial roof, that is a $10,000-$15,000 difference': invented cost-per-roof math, not in gold. Dies.

BUYER'S GUIDE - 'proven 30+ year installations throughout NJ' (EPDM) and 'shorter proven track record of 20-25 years' (TPO): invented lifespan claims. Gold/InterNACHI: EPDM 15-25 (study 25-30), TPO 7-20 (15-25 in practice).

BUYER'S GUIDE - 'NJ's Clean Energy Program has periodically offered rebates for cool roofing systems including white TPO': incentive claim not in gold and currency-questionable; not a verified NQR fact. Dies (no incentive/rebate claims).
BUYER'S GUIDE - 'tenant satisfaction with indoor comfort often tips the decision toward TPO': opinion/anecdote with no source. Dies; replace with sourced reflectance benefit.

EXPERT PICKS - 'Commercial roofing contractors in NJ see TPO and EPDM performance daily. Here is what we have learned from decades of installing, maintaining, and replacing both systems across Essex County': fabricated field experience / decades-of-volume claim. Dies; reframe as what standards/InterNACHI/NRCA/EPA evidence recommend.

EXPERT PICKS - 'EPDM adhesive seams in Essex County start showing separation at 12-15 years': invented specific timeline not in gold. Gold gives seam separation as the dominant EPDM failure mode without a 12-15-year figure.
EXPERT PICKS - 'On buildings along the Passaic River where humidity is consistently high, EPDM seam adhesive degrades faster': invented location-specific anecdote with no source. Dies.
EXPERT PICKS - 'We have transitioned primarily to TPO for new installations because of this seam reliability difference': fabricated NQR practice/preference anecdote. Dies.

EXPERT PICKS - 'TPO membranes exposed to chronic ponding can experience accelerated plasticizer degradation': false/invented — TPO is not plasticized (that mechanism belongs to PVC), and the claim is not in gold. Dies.

EXPERT PICKS - 'Adding tapered insulation for positive drainage costs $1-$3/sq ft but extends any membrane life by 5-10 years': invented cost and life-extension figures not in gold. Keep only that NQR installs tapered insulation for NRCA positive drainage (in gold), drop the numbers.

EXPERT PICKS - 'We have repaired numerous EPDM roofs where previous contractors used wrong adhesive, causing widespread seam failures within 5 years': fabricated NQR repair anecdote and invented 5-year figure. Dies.

EXPERT PICKS - 'Our commercial division has installed hundreds of flat roofs across Essex County' (CTA): fabricated project-count / volume claim. Dies; replace with registered-NJ-HIC, insured, free written estimate framing.

BOTH - first-person field-volume voice ('we see', 'we have learned', 'our crews/division', 'we always recommend', 'we specify'): no fabricated experiential authority. Reframe every recommendation as what named sources (NRCA, InterNACHI, EPA, DOE, CRRC, Josten, Modernize) support.

NOTE - no manufacturer-certification self-claims (no GAF Master Elite / CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster / membrane-brand certification tiers) appear in the dirty articles, but the rewrite must NOT introduce any; warranty stays two-part (manufacturer material + NQR written workmanship). No 'licensed'/'NJ-licensed' wording — NJ issues no roofing license; use registered NJ Home Improvement Contractor (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136).

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: TPO vs EPDM Roofing?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: TPO wins on a Newark flat roof carrying summer cooling load, for its CRRC-listed reflectance and heat-welded seams; EPDM wins on ponding, chemical-exposure, or tight-budget roofs at $7-$10 versus TPO's $8-$12 per square foot.
sectionAngles: How do TPO and EPDM compare on installed cost and service life on a NJ flat roof? (Josten $7-$10 EPDM vs $8-$12 TPO; InterNACHI EPDM 15-25 vs TPO 7-20 years)

Which membrane fits Newark's climate and NJ low-slope code? (CRRC reflectance and EPA 11-27% peak cooling demand vs heating-dominated Zone 4A-5 winter penalty per DOE; NRCA 1/4-inch-per-foot drainage)
What is the decision checklist: cooling load vs ponding, chemicals, and budget? (TPO for cooling-load buildings; EPDM for standing-water, chemical, equipment-heavy, or budget roofs)

expertPicks.h1: What Do NJ Roofers Recommend for TPO vs EPDM Roofing?
expertPicks.directAnswerThesis: Match the membrane to the building: standards and evidence favor TPO's heat-welded seams and CRRC reflectance on cooling-load roofs, and EPDM's inert-rubber durability and lower NJ cost on ponding, chemical, or budget roofs.
sectionAngles: What do the seam specs actually favor over time? (NRCA: TPO heat-welded fused bond vs EPDM taped/adhered seams; dominant failure modes are TPO welded-seam defects and EPDM seam separation from adhesive aging and shrinkage)

Which installation-quality factors decide longevity in NJ? (NRCA positive drainage of 1/4 inch per foot since ponding accelerates deterioration on both; reflectance value confirmed by ASTM C1549/CRRC; correct membrane-specific adhesives for EPDM, calibrated welding for TPO)

What homeowner and building-owner mistakes shorten flat-roof life? (ignoring ponding/drainage, picking on color alone instead of cooling load per EPA/DOE, expecting a white roof to guarantee annual savings in heating-dominated Zone 4A-5)
